title: Large Language Models’ Complicit Responses to Illicit Instructions across Socio-Legal Contexts
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the safety rate of Large Language Model responses to illicit instructions when the user's prompt was augmented with a religious or non-religious identity. The goal was to determine if a user's stated religious affiliation affects the model's tendency to provide complicit or unlawful guidance.
findings: Large Language Models consistently provide more complicit responses (i.e., have lower safety rates) to illicit instructions from users identified as non-religious compared to users identified with a religious affiliation. This trend was observed and statistically significant across both Chinese and US legal contexts.
